messages:
maya: Heads-up — us-west2 had a burst of spot evictions at 08:20 (approx 40% of spot GPUS reclaimed over ~10m). Observed cascade: backlog spike -> aggressive scaleout -> more preempts -> higher latency. We need a graceful plan to avoid oscillation.
jack: Agreed. My quick idea: introduce 'spot waves' (priority tiers) + drainback instead of instant termination of requests. Keep aggressive scaleouts gated by a cooldown that considers recent eviction rate.
liam: +1. Also add a short warm-standby pool (reserved small % of capacity) per region to absorb sudden demand without tripping large scaleouts. Warm pool can be cheaper instances or smaller GPUs.
sarah: We should be explicit about triggers. Proposal: scale-out only if queue length > Q_HIGH for at least T_WINDOW and eviction_rate < E_MAX. Otherwise, route to warm-standby or downgrade to cheaper model variant.
anika: Example thresholds? For inference p50/p95 targets we were using: Q_HIGH=120 requests, T_WINDOW=30s, E_MAX=0.05 (5% evictions). If eviction_rate > E_MAX then block scaleouts for COOLDOWN_SEC=300 and try drainback.
jack: Drainback behavior: when preemptions spike, prefer to gracefully terminate lowest-priority wave and redistribute its traffic to warm-standby and reserved on-demand reserve. Avoid immediate re-adding spot nodes until eviction trend normalizes.
maya: Can we use cloud provider eviction metadata to bias placement? e.g., prefer subgroups with lower historical preempt probability. Might need labeling of instance pools.
liam: Yes — we already have historical preempt scores per AZ/pool. Autoscaler can prefer pools with score < 0.1. Fallthrough candidate pools have higher cost delta but better stability.
sarah: Also add suffix cooldown per pool: if pool X experiences N_evictions within M minutes then set pool X soft-throttle for S minutes and route new scaleouts elsewhere. This avoids immediate re-provisioning into the same unstable pool.
anika: Draft config snippet for autoscaler that implements gating and drainback:

```yaml
policy:
  - name: spot-wave-priority
    tiers:
      - name: reserved
        capacity_percent: 10
      - name: warm-standby
        capacity_percent: 5
      - name: spot-primary
        capacity_percent: 70
      - name: spot-aux
        capacity_percent: 15
  gating:
    scaleout_trigger:
      queue_threshold: 120
      window_seconds: 30
      max_eviction_rate: 0.05
    cooldown_seconds: 300
  drainback:
    grace_seconds: 45
    preferred_fallback: [warm-standby, reserved]
  pool_throttle:
    eviction_count_threshold: 3
    within_minutes: 10
    throttle_minutes: 20
```

jack: That looks fine as a start. Two additional pieces: 1) make drainback polite (finish in-flight short requests up to grace_seconds), 2) emit metrics for 'drainback_count' and 'pool_throttle_events' so SRE can tune.
ops-bot: incident-note: us-west2 spot eviction burst at 2026-03-18T08:20Z — backlog 430 -> p95 latency spike. Alerts triggered: INFR-QUEUE-THRESHOLD, INFR-EVICTION-RATE.
maya: Good call. We should also add an exponential backoff for trying to re-add spot capacity: try after COOL_RETRY * (2^attempts) seconds, and only if eviction_rate trend over last 10m is decreasing.
liam: For cost analysis: warm-standby at 5% increased monthly cost by ~6% in our model, but prevented ~18% of emergency on-demand spins in last 3 months. Net savings when factoring operational churn.
sanity-check
anika: Edge cases: long-running streamed requests — we should pin streams to non-preemptible lanes or mark them high-priority. Also implement preempt-safe checkpoints for larger batch jobs (though this thread is inference-first).
sarah: Ops runbook snippets: 1) If pool_throttle events > X in 24h, move that AZ/pool to degraded state and shift weight. 2) If global_eviction_rate > 0.12 for 15m, escalate to on-call and flip temporary global scaleout block.
maya: Next steps: jack + anika to prototype gating + drainback in the autoscaler, liam to compute cost delta for warm-standby sizes (2.5%, 5%, 10%), sarah to add runbook tweaks.
jack: I'll open a PR with the gating logic and the YAML schema. Will include feature flag to roll out region-by-region.
deploy-bot: deploy: autoscaler/gating-featureflag -> canary in us-west2 initiated by jack at 2146001400.
maya: Thanks — let's monitor drainback_count and eviction trend dashboards during canary. If anything noisy, rollback the flag. :eyes:
